lesson.title: Review: Writing a Complete Persuasive Piece
lesson.subject: ela

contentBlocks.text: All week you've built one piece at a time: claim, reasons and evidence, a counterargument response, and organization. Today, write the complete, finished piece.

Quick review: a strong persuasive piece states a specific claim (Day 1), supports it with reasons and concrete evidence (Day 2), addresses a counterargument (Day 3), and is organized with linking words in a clear order (Day 4). Using your Day 4 outline, write out your complete persuasive piece as full sentences and paragraphs. End with a strong concluding statement that restates your position with new energy, not just a repeat of your opening claim.
You just wrote a complete, genuinely sophisticated persuasive piece — with a claim, evidence, a counterargument, and strong organization. This is real, advanced persuasive writing.

objectives: Recall all components of a strong persuasive piece: claim, reasons/evidence, counterargument, organization
Write a complete persuasive piece combining the week's separate components into full paragraphs
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Do the quick walk-through review of all 4 days together, out loud.
2. Have the child write their finished persuasive piece using their Day 4 outline as a guide.
3. Read the finished piece aloud together, checking it includes all required components.
4. Celebrate finishing a real, sophisticated piece of persuasive writing.
5. Note this same claim/evidence/counterargument/organization structure will apply to future persuasive and argumentative writing units.
differentiationTips: Struggling: allow the piece to remain closer to an organized list of sentences rather than requiring full paragraph transitions
Ready for more: ask them to add a second counterargument-and-response pair beyond the one from Day 3
This is a genuine finished-writing milestone — more sophisticated than Grade 3's simpler opinion paragraph, worth explicitly celebrating as a step up
teacherGuide.answerKey: Answers will vary — check the finished piece includes a specific claim, at least 2 reasons with evidence, a counterargument with response, linking words, and a strong concluding statement (not a verbatim repeat of the opening claim).
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Synthesizes the full week's Common Core Grade 5 Writing standards (W.5.1a-d) into one complete persuasive piece, matching the course's own 'persuasive writing' description as the foundational genre skill.
